pr_title: add option for far plane culling (#8173)
pr_body:
# Objective

- Adds option to `Projection` for far plane culling, and updates `check_visibility` to perform culling based on this property
- Before this change Frustum Culling would only account for near, left, right, top, and bottom planes with no trivial user facing overrides
- "Fixes #8173"

## Solution

- In addition to providing the option and updating check visibility, the new `use_far_culling: bool` defaults to false to prevent breaking changes
- with the use_far_culling option enabled, the perspective projection will behave more like the defaults in Godot, Unity, and Unreal where all 6 planes of the frustum are used for visibility tests
- this can lead to performance improvements on weaker targets like mobile with minimal effort

---

## Changelog

- Added use_far_culling option for camera_3d projections. Consider enabling this option for a quick performance boost for weaker targets until occlusion culling is ready.

## Example
Checkout https://github.com/NotoriousENG/bevy_cull_bug/tree/feature/fix_example and build against this PR for bevy to see in action
 
Image Showing Far Plane culling is working
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32341612/227695870-f1a0bd56-9f5d-429e-bfb1-04545bf918d4.png)

**Welcome**, new contributor!

  Please make sure you've read our [contributing guide](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and we look forward to reviewing your pull request shortly ✨
Is there anything missing for this PR?

It looks like your PR is a breaking change, but you didn't provide a migration guide.

  Could you add some context on what users should update when this change get released in a new version of Bevy?
  It will be used to help writing the migration guide for the version. Putting it after a `## Migration Guide` will help it get automatically picked up by our tooling.

> Is there anything missing for this PR?

I think there was no consensus as what default value will be set for the `far` variable. AFAICS it'll be 0.0 now, instead of the previous value of 1000.0. Someone suggested using a constant to store this value which sounds sensible to me (so it can be used as `.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_FAR_VALUE)`).
I approved before noticing there are conflicts. Assuming these are fixed I think this PR is ready.
Also @NotoriousENG could you add a Migration Guide section to the PR description that tells people to wrap the far value in an Option. It's a pretty obvious migration but better safe than sorry.

comments:
This is intentional. Our perspective projection has an infinite far plane and apparently games no longer do far plane culling, instead you manage what is loaded/visible in your scene separately. Because the projection has no far plane, you can see as far as you have things loaded.

However, when identifying which meshes are affected by individual lights, entities are culled against the far planes of the light projections.

> This is intentional. Our perspective projection has an infinite far plane and apparently games no longer do far plane culling, instead you manage what is loaded/visible in your scene separately. Because the projection has no far plane, you can see as far as you have things loaded.
1. Is this really intentional?
 * Bevy 0.6 had frustum culling as highlight when released
 * PerspectiveProjection has a far field? Why would a system override this and treat it as infinite?
2. What Games no longer use frustum culling?
 * [Godot](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/performance/optimizing_3d_performance.html), [Unity](https://docs.unity3d.com/2023.2/Documentation/Manual/UnderstandingFrustum.html), and [Unreal Engine](https://docs.unrealengine.com/4.26/en-US/RenderingAndGraphics/VisibilityCulling/) all support frustum culling by default
 * As do Rockstar, Creation, other more closed/specialized engines, this is typically one of the first steps you can do to increase rendering perfomance.
> However, when identifying which meshes are affected by individual lights, entities are culled against the far planes of the light projections.
1. Does this mean lighting would still be calculated for invisible objects? Doesn't this hurt performance? I don't think this would be good practice?

We still have frustum culling, we just don’t cull against any far plane for the camera view frustum. We still cull against the near, left, right, top, and bottom planes. Over time we will add occlusion culling so if objects block other objects, those blocked objects are culled too.

For lights the culling is for shadow mapping and it’s more complicated but the short version is that we try to cull meshes that don’t affect the shadow casting of the light into the scene. So if there are objects between the light and the visible scene where shadows can be cast, they should be rendered into the shadow map.

Thank you for your explanations! Especially for clearing up the shadow mapping. Knowing the other planes are culled is good too! :)

Is the far value of the view frustum unused then? 

Could it be changed to be used for culling? 
* it's not really intuitive that bevy doesn't cull on the far plane
  * in Godot, Unity, and Unreal replicating this example will have culling on the far plane
  * new users may think this is a bug, especially as this kills performance on weak hardware.
  
Regarding the ability to not have this far culling at the same time
* Making it large or adding a property for infinite far plane would match current behavior?
We could possibly make it optional for perspective projections.

review_comments: I think if the far plane is `None` then far could be `f32::INFINITY`. But it would be better to just not test against the far plane in that case.
